events.title: The 1971 Bangladesh Genocide and US Complicity
events.summary: The systematic mass murder and genocidal campaign conducted by the Pakistan Armed Forces and allied paramilitary death squads (Razakars, Al-Badr) against the Bengali population in East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) between March and December 1971. Despite detailed internal warnings of selective genocide from US Consul General Archer Blood in Dhaka ('The Blood Telegram'), US President Richard Nixon and National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger actively shielded Pakistan's military dictator, General Yahya Khan. The Nixon administration bypassed congressional arms embargoes by orchestrating covert third-party weapons transfers via Jordan, Iran, and Turkey, provided diplomatic cover at the United Nations, and deployed the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Enterprise (Task Force 74) to the Bay of Bengal in an effort to deter Indian intervention.

events.title: The 1964 Brazilian Coup d'État (Operation Brother Sam)
events.summary: The military overthrow of democratically elected Brazilian President João Goulart on March 31–April 1, 1964, orchestrated by right-wing Brazilian armed forces generals with direct diplomatic, logistical, and military backing from the United States under 'Operation Brother Sam.' Alarmed by Goulart's progressive domestic reforms—including land redistribution, literacy enfranchisement, and restrictions on foreign corporate profit remittances—the Kennedy and Johnson administrations actively supported anti-government conspirators. Declassified White House recordings confirm President Lyndon B. Johnson ordered the deployment of a US Navy aircraft carrier strike group, destroyers, ammunition, and aviation fuel to the Brazilian coast to intervene if rebel forces met resistance. The coup installed a 21-year military dictatorship that dissolved congress, institutionalized torture, and pioneered transnational state-terror networks later integrated into Operation Condor.

events.title: Operation Tradewinds, Castle Bank & CIA Offshore Shielding
events.era: Cold War Offshore Banking & Intelligence Conduits
events.summary: The landmark collision between federal tax enforcement and the intelligence community, in which an IRS investigation into hundreds of ultra-wealthy Americans evading taxes through Castle Bank & Trust in the Bahamas was shut down after the CIA intervened to protect its secret covert action funding conduits, setting the stage for 50 years of explosive offshore wealth concentration.

events.title: The Expulsion of the Chagossians and Diego Garcia Military Base
events.summary: The systematic forced expulsion and deportation of the entire indigenous Chagossian population (between 1,500 and 2,000 people) from the Chagos Archipelago—most notably the central atoll of Diego Garcia—in the Indian Ocean by the British government on behalf of the United States. Under a secret 1966 bilateral agreement, the UK agreed to 'depopulate' the islands to facilitate the construction of a major US naval and air base (Naval Support Facility Diego Garcia) in exchange for an unannounced $14 million discount on Polaris submarine-launched nuclear missiles. British officials deliberately deceived the United Nations and the public by falsely categorizing the multi-generational Chagossian population as temporary contract laborers. In 2019, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that the detachment of the archipelago and the expulsion were illegal under international law.

events.title: The 1973 Chilean Coup d'État and the Overthrow of Salvador Allende
events.summary: The violent military overthrow of Chile's democratically elected socialist President Salvador Allende on September 11, 1973, orchestrated by the Chilean Armed Forces under General Augusto Pinochet following a multi-year covert destabilization and economic warfare campaign directed by US President Richard Nixon, National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger, and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA Project FUBELT). The coup inaugurated a 17-year military dictatorship characterized by mass executions, concentration camps, systematic torture, and the transnational state-terror network known as Operation Condor.

events.title: The 1960–1961 Congo Coup and the Assassination of Patrice Lumumba
events.summary: The covert overthrow and assassination of the Democratic Republic of the Congo's first democratically elected Prime Minister, Patrice Lumumba, orchestrated by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and Belgian intelligence services between July 1960 and January 1961. Driven by determination to maintain Western control over the Congo's vital strategic mineral wealth—specifically the Shinkolobwe uranium deposits that fueled the Manhattan Project's atomic bombs, as well as cobalt and copper—CIA Director Allen Dulles designated Lumumba's removal an 'urgent and prime objective.' The CIA deployed lethal biological toxins to Léopoldville, subsidized military opposition figures including Army Chief of Staff Colonel Joseph-Désiré Mobutu, and facilitated Lumumba's abduction and delivery to Belgian-backed Katangese secessionist firing squads, inaugurating 32 years of kleptocratic military dictatorship under Mobutu Sese Seko.

events.title: The 1975–1999 East Timor Genocide and Western Complicity
events.summary: The 24-year military invasion, occupation, and genocidal campaign waged by the Indonesian Armed Forces against the population of Timor-Leste (East Timor) between December 1975 and late 1999. The invasion was initiated hours after US President Gerald Ford and Secretary of State Henry Kissinger met with Indonesian dictator Suharto in Jakarta, giving explicit advance approval. The United States provided approximately 90% of the weaponry used in the initial assault—including OV-10 Bronco counter-insurgency aircraft, M16 rifles, and naval support—while utilizing diplomatic influence in the United Nations Security Council to obstruct enforcement of international resolutions calling for Indonesia's withdrawal.

events.title: The 2023–Present Gaza War, Regional Escalation, and International Supply Chains
events.summary: The ongoing conventional military offensive conducted by the Israel Defense Forces ('Operation Swords of Iron') in the Gaza Strip following the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel. The campaign has been characterized by unprecedented levels of aerial bombardment, total naval, land, and aerial blockade, mass forced displacement of over 1.9 million people (85–90% of the population), and widespread destruction of civic, educational, and medical infrastructure. The operation has been directly sustained by emergency diplomatic protection, logistical airlifts, and arms transfers from the United States (tens of thousands of precision bombs, 155mm shells, and bunker busters) and the United Kingdom (F-35 component manufacturing and daily RAF Akrotiri aerial surveillance flights). Crucially, the campaign is powered by an extensive corporate technological architecture: sovereign cloud computing and AI under 'Project Nimbus' (Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services), battlefield AI battle-management software from Palantir Technologies, enterprise cloud systems from Microsoft, and military networking hardware from Cisco and HPE. Whistleblower intelligence reports documented the deployment of automated AI targeting programs—notably 'Lavender' (generating kill lists of tens of thousands of suspected targets with pre-authorized civilian collateral thresholds), 'The Gospel' (generating structural targets at industrial speed), and 'Where's Daddy?' (tracking targets to family homes before striking)—prompting formal genocide proceedings at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and corporate complicity filings at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

events.title: The 1954 Guatemalan Coup d'État (Operation PBSuccess)
events.summary: The covert paramilitary and psychological warfare operation planned and executed by the United States Central Intelligence Agency (Operation PBSuccess) that overthrew the democratically elected government of Guatemalan President Jacobo Árbenz. Orchestrated in direct defense of the commercial landholdings of the American United Fruit Company (UFCO) following Árbenz's progressive agrarian land reform (Decree 900), the coup installed a brutal military dictatorship under Carlos Castillo Armas, rolling back land reforms, outlawing labor unions, and precipitating a 36-year civil war in which over 200,000 predominantly indigenous Mayan civilians were murdered or disappeared by US-backed military regimes.

events.title: Guatemalan Maya Genocide & Operation Sofía
events.era: Cold War Proxy Conflicts & State Terror
events.summary: The systematic campaign of mass slaughter, scorched-earth destruction, and forced displacement perpetrated by the Guatemalan military dictatorship under General Efraín Ríos Montt against the indigenous Maya-Ixil and Maya-K'iche' populations, formally recognized as acts of genocide by the UN-sponsored Historical Clarification Commission and Guatemalan criminal courts.

events.title: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom
events.summary: The illegal overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani and the sovereign constitutional monarchy of the Hawaiian Kingdom by a syndicate of American sugar barons and corporate elites, executed with the direct complicity of US diplomatic minister John L. Stevens and 162 armed US Marines and sailors from the USS Boston, establishing the foundational prototype for 20th-century American regime change operations.

events.title: The 1965–1966 Indonesian Mass Killings and CIA Involvement
events.summary: The systematic anti-communist purge and extermination of between 500,000 and 1,000,000+ suspected leftists, trade unionists, peasant organizers, and ethnic Chinese in Indonesia, orchestrated by the Indonesian military under Major General Suharto with covert financial, logistical, and intelligence assistance from the United States government and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). Declassified diplomatic cables confirmed that US Embassy officials compiled and provided comprehensive execution lists containing thousands of names of Communist Party of Indonesia (PKI) leaders and members to Indonesian army death squads, while US radio equipment and covert funds facilitated nationwide extermination operations.

events.title: The 1953 Iranian Coup d'État (Operation Ajax / TPAJAX)
events.summary: The covert overthrow of the democratically elected Prime Minister of Iran, Mohammad Mosaddegh, orchestrated by the United States Central Intelligence Agency (Operation TPAJAX) and the British Secret Intelligence Service (Operation Boot). The coup restored absolute monarchical rule under Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi following Mosaddegh's nationalization of Iran's oil industry, which had been monopolized by the British Anglo-Iranian Oil Company.

events.title: The 2003 Invasion of Iraq (Operation Iraqi Freedom)
events.summary: The conventional military invasion and occupation of the Republic of Iraq by a multinational coalition led by the United States and the United Kingdom. The operation overthrew the Ba'athist government of Saddam Hussein based on stated justifications concerning unverified stockpiles of weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and alleged ties to al-Qaeda, neither of which were substantiated by subsequent exhaustive post-invasion searches.

events.title: Korean War Aerial Bombing Campaign & Civilian Massacres
events.summary: The catastrophic air bombardment campaign conducted by the US Far East Air Force destroying an estimated 85% of all building structures across North Korea, accompanied by targeted destruction of agricultural irrigation dams and widespread civilian massacres executed by US troops and allied South Korean forces (including No Gun Ri and the Bodo League massacres).

events.title: The 2011 NATO Intervention in Libya and the Fall of Gaddafi
events.summary: A multi-nation military intervention in Libya led by the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)—under operational command of the United States, France, and the United Kingdom—between March and October 2011 (Operation Unified Protector / Operation Odyssey Dawn). Ostensibly authorized under United Nations Security Council Resolution 1973 to establish a no-fly zone and protect civilians in Benghazi, NATO rapidly converted the mission into an aggressive regime-change air campaign, executing over 9,600 strike sorties, providing covert ground arms transfers and special forces advisers to rebel militias, and destroying the command infrastructure of the Libyan state. The intervention culminated on October 20, 2011, when a US Predator drone and French fighter jets struck the fleeing convoy of long-time Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi in Sirte, leading to his capture, torture, and extrajudicial killing by rebel fighters. The collapse of the Libyan government precipitated a decade of catastrophic civil war, institutional fragmentation, the proliferation of heavy weaponry across the Sahel, and the re-emergence of open-air chattel slave markets.

events.title: Operation Condor: The Transnational State Terror Network
events.summary: A covert, formalized campaign of transnational political repression, cross-border abductions, systematic torture, and extrajudicial assassinations coordinated by the military intelligence agencies of South America's Southern Cone (Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia, and Brazil) between 1975 and the mid-1980s. The network operated with technical telecommunications infrastructure (the Condortel encrypted communications network based in the US Panama Canal Zone), surveillance data sharing, and high-level diplomatic shielding provided by the United States Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and Secretary of State Henry Kissinger. Condor operatives deployed specialized hit squads ('Phase III') to eliminate prominent political exiles, constitutionalist military officers, and human rights defenders across Latin America, North America, and Europe.

events.title: US Military Invasion of Panama (Operation Just Cause)
events.era: Post-Cold War Unipolarity & Latin American Interventions
events.summary: The massive military invasion of Panama launched by the Bush administration involving over 27,000 US troops, heavy artillery, and air strikes to capture de facto military ruler General Manuel Noriega (a long-time CIA asset), resulting in the devastation of the densely populated civilian neighborhood of El Chorrillo and formal condemnation by the UN General Assembly and the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights.

events.title: The Sabra and Shatila Massacre (September 1982)
events.summary: The slaughter of between 700 and 3,500 predominantly Palestinian and Lebanese Shiite civilians in the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps in West Beirut by Lebanese Christian Phalangist (Kataeb) militia forces, conducted while the perimeter was controlled and illuminated by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) under Defense Minister Ariel Sharon following the 1982 Israeli invasion of Lebanon.

events.title: The 1963 South Vietnamese Coup and Assassination of Ngo Dinh Diem
events.summary: The military overthrow and summary execution of South Vietnamese President Ngo Dinh Diem and his brother Ngo Dinh Nhu on November 1–2, 1963, orchestrated by senior generals of the Army of the Republic of Vietnam (ARVN) with explicit advance authorization, operational encouragement, and financial backing from the United States government and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). Facing global public outrage over the Diem regime's brutal crackdowns on Buddhist monks and civilian dissidents, and convinced that Diem was losing the war against the Viet Cong, the Kennedy administration issued 'Cable 243' authorizing US Ambassador Henry Cabot Lodge Jr. and CIA operative Lucien Conein to signal to rebel generals that Washington would support Diem's ouster and maintain full military and economic aid. The coup eliminated South Vietnam's chief political figure, locked the United States into direct moral ownership of the war, and precipitated a series of unstable military juntas that prompted massive conventional US military escalation.

events.title: US Covert Operations, the 2002 Coup Attempt, and Economic Sanctions Against Venezuela
events.summary: A multi-decade campaign of diplomatic isolation, covert destabilization, and comprehensive unilateral economic sanctions waged by successive United States administrations against the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. Key episodes include the April 2002 military coup attempt against democratically elected President Hugo Chávez backed by US-funded opposition entities, followed from 2017 onward by sweeping financial and petroleum embargoes ('Maximum Pressure') that crippled Venezuela's oil export revenues, restricted life-saving imports of food and medicine, and caused an estimated 40,000+ excess civilian deaths according to peer-reviewed economic and United Nations human rights studies.

events.title: The Vietnam War, Indochina Bombing Campaigns, and Chemical Defoliation
events.summary: The massive military intervention conducted by the United States Armed Forces in Southeast Asia from 1964 to 1975, initiated under the pretext of the fabricated Gulf of Tonkin incident. The conflict involved the deployment of over 540,000 American combat troops, the expenditure of more than 7.5 million tons of aerial munitions across Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia (more than double the total tonnage used in World War II), widespread chemical ecocide via Agent Orange dioxin defoliants manufactured by Dow Chemical and Monsanto, and CIA targeted assassination operations (the Phoenix Program). Demographic and governmental inquiries estimate total deaths between 2 and 3.8 million people, including up to 2 million civilians.
